--- title: "Your First Quarto Report" --- ## When is Lake Mendota frozen? The Wisconsin State Climatology Office decides each winter.
For Mendota, one of their rules is a bit unusual: - Can you row a boat from [Picnic Point]{.uwred} to [Maple Bluff]{.uwred}? - If not, the lake is frozen.
The story, handed down by oral tradition: - UW limnologists E. A. Birge and Chancey Juday were often out on the lake in a rowboat - The ice along that line decided whether they could row [a case of beer]{.uwred} to their friends in Maple Bluff -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## Our data Observers have recorded ice on Lake Mendota every winter since the 1850s.
You downloaded them to `data/mendota_ice.csv`, one row per winter: - `winter`: the winter, e.g., `1855-56` - `year`: the year that winter ended - `ice_days`: days the lake was frozen
171 winters, from 1855-56 to 2025-26. - The question for our report: is ice cover declining? -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## What we will build One file, `report.qmd`, with: - A [YAML]{.uwred} header: title, author, date, format - Text written in [markdown]{.uwred}: headings, paragraphs, lists - [Code chunks]{.uwred} that load the data and draw a figure - [Inline R]{.uwred}: numbers in sentences, computed from the data
We will render it after each step so you can see what changed. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## Create the file In the terminal, move into your repo and create an empty file: ```bash cd ~/github/mendota_ice touch report.qmd ```
Then open `report.qmd` in RStudio: - Use the [Files]{.uwred} pane, or File → Open File - It is a plain-text file, like an `.R` script -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## The YAML ("Yet Another Markup Language") header Type this at the very top of `report.qmd`: ```yaml --- title: "Ice Cover on Lake Mendota" author: "Your Name" date: today format: html --- ```
The header sits between two lines of `---` - Each line is a `key: value` pair - `format: html` says what to build - `date: today` fills in the date each time you render -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## Render it Back in the terminal: ```bash quarto render report.qmd ```
Quarto writes [`report.html`]{.uwred} next to your `.qmd`. - Open it in your browser - In RStudio: click it in the Files pane → View in Web Browser
So far, just a title, author, and date. - Each time you change the `.qmd`, render again and reload the page -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## Markdown: headings, text, and lists Below the YAML header, add: ```markdown ## Background Lake Mendota has been watched for ice since the **1850s**. For each winter, the record notes: - the date the lake froze - the date it opened ## Ice cover over time ```
- `##` is a section heading, `###` a subsection - Put a space after the `#` - Start at `##`; the YAML `title` is already the top level - `**bold**` makes text [bold]{.uwred} - A line starting with `- ` is a list item -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## Blank lines matter If you leave out the blank line before the list (Don't do this step today) ```markdown For each winter, the record notes: - the date the lake froze - the date it opened ```
You get one run-on paragraph: > For each winter, the record notes: - the date the lake froze - the date it opened
Markdown needs a [blank line]{.uwred}: - before a list - before and after a heading - between paragraphs -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## Your turn ::: {.callout-wide} ::: {.callout-important} # Try it 1. Add the headings, text, and list from the last few slides 2. Render with `quarto render report.qmd` 3. Reload `report.html` and check that the list is a list 4. (Try later) Remove the blank line above the list items, render again, and see what breaks ::: ::: -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## Code chunks R code goes in a [code chunk]{.uwred}: ```{{r}} #| label: setup library(tidyverse) ice <- read_csv("data/mendota_ice.csv") ```
- Starts with ```` ```{r} ```` and ends with ```` ``` ```` - Lines starting with `#|` are [chunk options]{.uwred} - `label` names the chunk (use snake_case; not always required but helps when debugging)
Add this chunk just below the YAML header, then render. - A [setup chunk]{.uwred} at the top loads packages and data for the whole document -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## Hide the messages Your readers do not need these in your report: - the tidyverse startup messages - the column messages from `read_csv()`
Add one option to the `setup` chunk: ```{{r}} #| label: setup #| message: false library(tidyverse) ice <- read_csv("data/mendota_ice.csv") ```
- `message: false` hides messages; the code still runs
Want to hide the chunk completely? - `include: false` runs the code but shows neither the code nor its output -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## Add a figure Under `## Ice cover over time`, add a chunk: ```{{r}} #| label: ice_plot ice |> ggplot(aes(x = year, y = ice_days)) + geom_line() + labs(x = "Winter (year it ended)", y = "Days of ice cover") + theme_minimal() ```
Render again. - Quarto runs the chunk and puts the figure right below the code - It also makes a `report_files/` folder for the image; more on that in the next unit -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## The figure in your report ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](02_report_files/figure-html/ice_plot-1.png){width=768} ::: :::
- Lots of year-to-year variation - But the trend is down -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## Inline R Do the work in a chunk: ```{{r}} #| label: means mean_1800s <- ice |> filter(year < 1900) |> pull(ice_days) |> mean() |> round() mean_recent <- ice |> filter(year >= 2000) |> pull(ice_days) |> mean() |> round() ```
Then put the results in your sentences with [inline R]{.uwred}: ```markdown Before 1900, the lake averaged `r mean_1800s` days of ice. Since 2000, it has averaged `r mean_recent`. ``` - Backtick, the letter `r`, a space, then R code, then a closing backtick - Keep inline R short; do the work in a chunk > Before 1900, the lake averaged 114 days of ice. Since 2000, it has averaged 81. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## Render runs in a fresh session In the RStudio [console]{.uwred}, run: ```r n_winters <- 171 ```
Then add a sentence to `report.qmd` and render: ```markdown There are `r n_winters` winters in the record. ```
`n_winters` exists in your console. - So why will this fail? -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## The error ``` Error in eval(parse_only(code), envir = envir) : object 'n_winters' not found Quitting from report.qmd:44-44 Execution halted ```
`quarto render` runs your code in a [fresh R session]{.uwred}. - It cannot see anything in your console - Not even chunks you ran in RStudio with the green ▶ - Every object the report uses must be created in the report
This is a feature: - If it renders, anyone with your `.qmd` and data can rebuild it
To fix it: - Create it in the report: add `n_winters <- nrow(ice)` to a chunk above the sentence -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## Your turn ::: {.callout-wide} ::: {.callout-important} # Try it 1. Add the `means` chunk and the two sentences with inline R 2. Add one more sentence: how many days of ice in the shortest winter on record? (Hint: `min(ice$ice_days)`) 3. Render, and check the numbers in `report.html` ::: ::: -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## Your turn: what to type Below the `means` chunk, your text should look like this: ```markdown Before 1900, the lake averaged `r mean_1800s` days of ice. Since 2000, it has averaged `r mean_recent`. The shortest winter on record had `r min(ice$ice_days)` days of ice. ```
> Before 1900, the lake averaged 114 days of ice. Since 2000, it has averaged 81. > > The shortest winter on record had 21 days of ice.
Still getting an error? - The sentences must come [after]{.uwred} the `means` chunk; code runs top to bottom - Delete or fix the `n_winters` sentence from the last demo -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ## Where we are We have: - Written a YAML header that sets the title, author, date, and format - Used markdown for headings, text, bold, and lists - Run R code in chunks, and hidden messages with chunk options - Put computed numbers in sentences with inline R - Seen that `quarto render` runs in a fresh session
::: {.callout-wide} ::: {.callout-important} # Next up Our report works, but it is spread across an HTML file and a folder. Next we will render it to [one self-contained file]{.uwred} and publish it online. ::: :::
